experiments.scope: The search of proof.md Section 4 on the exact sha3-256-r14-prefix-v1 hash, run end to end at width 22. experiments/ls1.py regenerates the claimed straight line of Section 3 from the generator's decisions (embedded plan; its two-address encoding must hash to the SHA-256 printed in Section 3.6, else the program stops), checks it against a plain 14-round implementation (two chained steps of 256 points), and executes it on Python integers: one integer holds a plane for all trials of the request (trial t in bits 256 t to 256 t + 255), trials never interact. Points are 22-bit values u (upper bits zero), the message is m(u) of Section 2 (128 bytes), and after every step the planes 22 to 255 are set to zero (with the labels of the starts below, the only difference from the full-size program). Per trial: 256 walks from starts rho + i (rho from SHAKE-256 of the trial seed; the full-size program labels trail i as t(i), Section 4), distinguished point = the 4 low image bits zero and the 3 bits above them, as a number, less than 5, no trail cut, at most 3,000 trails and 400 steps per attempt, a table end -> trail number, restarts, and the replay of Section 4 (the stored trail measured by walking it to its distinguished point with every 16th point kept as a checkpoint, the new trail walked once, the segment of the merge lock-stepped; trails of more than 256 evaluations refused) with the plain implementation. It returns two different messages whose 14-round digests agree on the 22 low bits. Each trial seed is prefixed by the 16-byte SALT of ls1.py, drawn once for this package. The run tests that the program and the search work at width 22; it does not test success at 256 bits.
experiments.hypothesis: Every trial returns two different messages m(a), m(b) whose digests agree on the 22 masked bits (bytes 0 and 1 and the low 6 bits of byte 2), found by walks, the table and the replay. Observations (untrusted): steps of the successful attempt, trails, attempts, table size, replayed evaluations. Our ideal-function control with the same parameters needs 20.47 steps on average (20,000 trials, sd 7.91). Nothing about the cost or the success probability at 256 bits is inferred from the run, and its frequencies are not used as statistical support.

experiments.scope: The same regenerated straight line at full width: per trial 256 uniform 256-bit points (SHAKE-256 of the trial seed), eight chained steps of the full program (2,048 evaluations per trial), and the first pair, in step-major order, of distinct evaluated inputs whose images agree on the 22 low bits; the two inputs are recomputed with the plain implementation and returned as messages m(a), m(b). A trial without such a pair returns two nulls. A success is a 22-bit partial match, not a collision. Each trial seed is prefixed by the 16-byte SALT of ls1.py, drawn once for this package. The run tests the regenerated straight line against the plain implementation and 22-bit agreement among 2,048 evaluations; it does not test a complete collision, 2^128 evaluations or the distinguished-point rate.
experiments.hypothesis: Model value, reported for comparison and not used: if the images of the 2,048 distinct evaluated inputs are uniform on 22 bits, a trial succeeds with probability 1 - prod_(i<2048)(1 - i/2^22) = 0.3934: about 100.7 of 256 successes, standard deviation 7.8. No probability or interval is inferred from the observed count. A wrong straight line would give digests that the organizer's recomputation does not match, and failed pairs.
